issues.description: Equal-ranked terminal states can overwrite newer terminal job data with stale older snapshots.
Unchanged detection ignores user, partition, submit/start, CPU, GPU, and exit_code changes, leaving corrected records stale.
Timestamp filtering and MAX calculations compare ISO strings lexicographically, which gives wrong results for timezone-offset timestamps.
Timezone-aware timestamps are accepted without normalization, feeding incompatible timestamp formats into SQLite text comparisons.
Rows with negative CPU/GPU counts and blank user or partition values are accepted as valid job records.
The schema has no CHECK constraints for nonnegative resources or non-empty required dimensions, so invalid parsed data is persisted.
connect() always creates the database and schema, which makes read-only report commands silently create empty databases for mistyped paths.
Report and top commands use the write/create database path instead of failing clearly when the requested database does not exist.
--n only has a lower bound, so very large values can trigger excessive query and output work.
No linting, formatting, typing, or coverage tooling is configured, leaving important correctness rules unenforced outside tests.
